script: "I joined a lit project with two 'geniuses', but they had NO IDEA what we were supposed to do". My. God. So, you guys, like, I was in this lit class, and we had to do this group project, and I am literally the only person in the class who gives a flying flip about actually doing the work. I mean, I am there for the tea, but the actual assignment? Not my jam. So, we get randomly grouped with two partners, and they're both so extra, like, they're obsessed with 1800s Scotland, and I am like, okay, how cute? We decide to do our project on Lord Byron and this dry-as-the-sand guy who's either high or possessed by the devil. I mean, it's not my fave, but I am about to take on the world for this group project. Here's the tea: my partners? Not even trying, bruh. They didn't read the material, not even the Lord Byron poem, and I am like, are you kidding me? I am over here trying to get my A-game on, and you two are slacking. So, I do the whole project myself, including the handouts. And then I get petty, like, I memorize everything, and for the worksheet, I write down bullet points that literally reveal nothing. I am like, I am not ratting you out, but I am not letting you get off scot-free either. The day of the presentation arrives, and I am like, bring it on. We stand up in front of the class, and I am passing out these worksheets, and my partners are nodding along like they're actually paying attention. I am like, this is too easy. I start talking about madness in 1800s Scotland, and I go in-depth on Lord Byron and the dry-as-the-sand guy. My partners are still nodding along, and I am like, okay, got it. The Q&A portion comes, and I am like, let's see if they're actually paying attention. I pause for a long time, and I am looking at them, like, come on, guys, answer this. But they're silent, and it's like, oh, I get it. They have no clue what's going on. I am like, the only one in this group who actually knows what's up. The professor pulls me aside after the fact and says he's going to grade me and my partners separately. I get an A, and they stop talking to me. Like, they're so salty, but honestly, I am here for it. I am like, you got played, besties, and now you're left with nothing but a bad grade and a broken friendship. Bless.
